name: Director, State Security Service v Olisa Agbakoba
summary: A leading case on the right to freedom of movement and the seizure of a citizen's passport by security agencies.
facts: Olisa Agbakoba's passport was seized by the State Security Service, preventing him from travelling. He challenged the seizure as a violation of his constitutional right to freedom of movement.
issues: Whether seizure of a citizen's passport without lawful authority violates freedom of movement.
What limits apply to security agencies when restricting travel.
holding: The Court treated passport seizure that stops a citizen travelling as engaging the constitutional freedom of movement, subject to the lawful limits set out in the Constitution. Students should confirm the exact holding in a licensed law report.
ratio: A Nigerian citizen's freedom of movement includes the practical ability to leave and return to Nigeria; arbitrary passport seizure by security agencies may therefore violate section 41 unless justified under a lawful constitutional limitation.
report_citation: See NWLR / law-report citation via a licensed law-report service

interpretations.body: Use this case to connect the abstract right in s.41 to a concrete state action (passport seizure). Ask: was there a law authorising the seizure, and did it fall within s.41(2) or other permitted limits?
